learning_objective: 🎯 Build complex sentences like a pro! Understand how clauses connect and master the flip between Active and Passive Voice.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A clause is a group of words that has a subject and a verb. An Independent Clause makes sense on its own ('I smiled'). A Dependent Clause needs help ('Because I was happy').
There are three types: 1. Noun Clause (acts like a noun), 2. Adjective Clause (describes a noun, usually starts with who/which/that), 3. Adverb Clause (answers when, where, why, how).
Active Voice: The Subject does the action ('The cat ate the mouse'). Passive Voice: The Subject receives the action ('The mouse was eaten by the cat').

1. Swap the Subject and Object. 2. Use the 'be' verb according to the tense (is/are/was/were/been/being). 3. ALWAYS use the 3rd form of the main verb (Past Participle). 4. Add 'by' before the new object.
In Passive Voice, if the 'doer' of the action is obvious or unknown, we drop them. E.g., 'The thief was arrested' (We don't need to say 'by the police' because it is obvious).

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ The News Anchor
fun_activity.instructions: News anchors love Passive Voice! Turn this active sentence into a passive news headline: 'The government will build a new bridge.' (Answer: 'A new bridge will be built (by the government).')

exam_tips: 📌 Passive voice ALWAYS uses the 3rd form (V3) of the verb. Never use V1 or V2 in passive.
📌 Present/Past Continuous active sentences ('is baking') need 'being' in passive ('is being baked').
📌 'Who' changes to 'By whom' in passive voice interrogative sentences.
quick_recap: ⭐ Independent clauses are joined by FANBOYS (For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So).
⭐ Dependent clauses usually start with words like Because, Although, If, When.
⭐ Passive voice is the standard tone used in formal writing and Report Writing.
